_comment: THE INDEX WRITER REGISTRY. Declarative manifest of every Azure AI Search index the fleet's retrieval tools can query, and -- critically -- WHAT WRITES IT. Consumed by setup/index-writer-gate.mjs (CI gate) and skills/azure-canary/canary.mjs (freshness canary). WHY IT EXISTS: on 2026-07-13 we found that `otchealth-brain` (67,645 docs) -- the ONLY index the gateway's brain_search queried, whose tool description told every agent 'Ground answers here and cite' -- HAD NO WRITER ANYWHERE. It was an ad-hoc one-time snapshot created outside both repos and outside IaC (git log -S across all 541 commits: the string first appears 2026-07-10, in a READER). It sat frozen for ~12 days while every agent grounded answers in it. Nothing caught it because (a) a job literally named `brain-reindex` ran green every 6h -- it actually refreshes memory-exec, and was named back when memory-exec WAS 'the brain' (company-brain/brain.mjs still labels it '(shared brain)'); (b) the only freshness signal we had was a doc-count FLOOR, and a frozen index never drops below a floor -- it stays identical forever; (c) expected-resources.json proves every JOB exists but asserts nothing about what a job WRITES. THE RULE THIS FILE ENFORCES: an index that any retrieval tool can query MUST have a registered writer that actually exists and is actually scheduled. If you wire a new index into a search tool, add it here, or index-writer-gate.mjs fails CI. If an index has no writer, it does not get to be a source of truth. 2026-07-20 PHASE-3-CUTOVER COMPLETION: the live service is now `otchealth-dataroom-s1` (chunked; the gateway's AZURE_SEARCH_ENDPOINT). The doc rooms on S1 are fed by NATIVE PULL-INDEXERS (`ixr-<room>`) not the librarian push-search jobs (push-search is retired on S1: its create/update path 400s on the chunked 2-key schema), and the S1 chunked schema carries NO per-doc timestamp field. So doc-room freshness is measured by the PULL-INDEXER's last successful run (`writer_indexer`), not a doc timestamp; memory-exec keeps its sortable `ts` field. The old Basic service `otchealth-dataroom-search` (a frozen 32k-doc pre-chunk subset, zero indexers, newest doc 2026-07-14) is decommissioned below.

indexes.note: The real shared brain. Written by the brain-reindex job (semantic.mjs reindex), NOT a native pull-indexer, and it carries a sortable `ts` field -- so freshness stays doc-timestamp based here. `brain-reindex` is NOT misnamed historically -- brain.mjs labels this index '(shared brain)'.

indexes.writer_source: S1 native pull-indexers ixr-commons-* (one per blob prefix), fed by the librarian/daily-digest index step that stages _TEXT sidecars to azure://otchealthcommons/company-journal
indexes.note: Fed by ~15 ixr-commons-* pull-indexers (bulletinseen/daily/docs/journal/recovery/research/state/vault/...). Freshness = newest successful run across those indexers < max_age AND none in a failed state. max_age is 48h not 4h: content only arrives when there is NEW material, so a quiet day is legitimately quiet.

indexes.writer_source: S1 native pull-indexer ixr-finance-cfo-source-docs, fed by the librarian-finance index step (stages source docs + _TEXT sidecars to blob)
indexes.note: MNPI ring. Source docs change slowly; a week of no new finance docs is normal, so max_age is generous. Freshness = the pull-indexer's last successful run.

indexes.writer_source: S1 native pull-indexer ixr-legal-company, fed by the librarian-legal-company index step
indexes.note: Attorney ring. Freshness = the pull-indexer's last successful run.

indexes.writer_source: S1 native pull-indexer ixr-legal-personal, fed by the librarian-legal-personal index step
indexes.note: ATTORNEY-PRIVILEGED. The canary reads ONLY the pull-indexer's run status + timestamp -- never document CONTENT -- so the freshness check does not breach the privilege wall.

indexes.writer_source: S1 native pull-indexer ixr-commerce-commerce-source-docs, fed by the librarian-commerce index step

decommissioning.note: NO WRITER, EVER. Ad-hoc one-time snapshot (~2026-07-01) created outside both repos and outside IaC; frozen at exactly 67,645 docs. Retired as a retrieval target by mcp-server PR #103 (brain_search now federates the live rooms above). DECOMMISSIONED 2026-07-14: verified a true orphan (brain_search federates the live rooms; no runtime code reads BRAIN_SEARCH_ENDPOINT/brain-search-key; fleet-backup iterates .indexes and excluded it), archived all 67,645 docs to azure://otchealthcommons/company-journal/_ARCHIVE/otchealth-brain-snapshot-2026-07-14.jsonl (2.91GB), then ARM-deleted the otchealth-brain-search service (azure-sp Owner; the gateway has no delete tool but the sandbox has direct ARM). Kept here as a permanent tombstone so index-writer-gate.mjs FAILS if any retrieval tool is ever re-pointed at this name. The dead BRAIN_SEARCH_ENDPOINT/BRAIN_SEARCH_KEY env still on the gateway is harmless (no runtime reader); remove on the next gateway env change.

decommissioning.status: DELETED 2026-07-20 (Basic service otchealth-dataroom-search removed; Phase-3 cutover orphan)
decommissioning.note: The pre-Phase-3 BASIC search service. Held a frozen 32k-doc PRE-CHUNK subset of the 15 rooms (finance-cfo-source-docs newest indexed_at 2026-07-14, 32,588 docs vs the live S1 chunked 224,087), had ZERO native indexers (nothing wrote it), and nothing read it (gateway AZURE_SEARCH_ENDPOINT + azure-search-endpoint secret + all skills = otchealth-dataroom-s1). It also carried the SAME index NAMES as S1 on the free semantic tier, whose exhausted 1000/mo quota was a latent 402 trap. DECOMMISSIONED 2026-07-20: verified a true frozen orphan (no writer, no reader, stale subset of S1), repointed the canary + fleet-backup registry to S1 first, then ARM-deleted the service (azure-sp Owner). No unique data lost (the real source docs live in Blob and are chunked into S1). Tombstoned so index-writer-gate.mjs FAILS if any tool is ever re-pointed at this name.
